name: transformer
description: A small decoder-only transformer forward pass, general in every dimension: n tokens, d_model, n_heads, n_kv shared K/V heads, d_k, d_ff, n_layers, pre- or post-norm, LayerNorm or RMSNorm, ReLU / GELU / SwiGLU, then the final norm, the tied unembedding, logits, temperature and probabilities. Its DEFAULT configuration is the lesson's toy — "the cat sat on the mat" at d_model=4, n_heads=2, d_k=2, one layer, layer 0 / head 0 carrying the hand-built projections — so every figure scenes 1-4 pin is unchanged; other weights are seeded deterministic tables, and any table can be replaced by a tensor slider named after it. Functions are available in the expression sandbox after importing this domain. Importing a domain does NOT require unsafe: true.
honesty_note: THE WEIGHTS ARE HAND-CONSTRUCTED FOR LEGIBILITY, NOT LEARNED. W_Q, W_K, W_V and the embedding table were chosen so that one head shows a clean subject-verb dependency: the verb 'sat' attends 97.09% of its softmax mass to the subject 'cat'. Real trained weights at d_model=4 produce noise, not interpretable heads. Any lesson using this domain MUST label the weights on screen as designed-for-teaching. A lesson advertising mathematical accuracy while presenting invented attention patterns as learned ones is dishonest at exactly the point it claims rigour.

implementation.toy_model: Default configuration: n=6 tokens, d_model=4, d_k=2 per head, n_heads=2, one layer, no norm. d_k != d_model is deliberate: it is what makes the 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling visibly about the HEAD dimension, which is the usual error. Every dimension can be changed by the tf_* sliders and a tf_emb table; the toy is only the default.
implementation.embedding_table: [[1,0,0,0] the, [0,1,0,0] cat, [0,0,1,0] sat, [0,0,0,1] on, [1,0,0,0] the, [0.5,0.5,0,0.5] mat]. Note 'the' occupies slots 0 and 4 with the IDENTICAL row — the two separate only once positional encoding is added.
implementation.positional_encoding: Standard sinusoidal, base 10000: PE[pos][2i] = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model)), PE[pos][2i+1] = cos(...). ADDED to the embedding, never concatenated — the width stays 4. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH RoPE: whenever s2_rope is on, this additive term is forced to zero regardless of s1_pe. RoPE REPLACES additive positional encoding; it does not stack on it. A model uses one scheme or the other, never both, and rotating a q that already carried a sinusoidal offset is an operation no model performs.
implementation.projections: Row-vector convention, q = x W_Q. Under that convention the ROWS of W are the images of the input basis directions. W_Q = [[0,0],[0,0],[3,0],[0,1]] reads input dims 2 and 3; W_K = [[0,0],[3,0],[0,0],[0,1]] reads dims 1 and 3; W_V = [[1,0],[0,1],[0,0],[0,0]] reads dims 0 and 1. Three different readings of ONE vector.
implementation.mask: Applied as an ADDITIVE -1e9 to the SCALED SCORES, before softmax. -1e9 stands in for -infinity so the renderer never sees a NaN; softmax's shift-invariance is what makes the substitution coherent.
implementation.cache: One shared cache of the forward pass, rebuilt only when a slider it READ has changed. Which sliders those are depends on the configuration (a two-layer model reads tf_wq_1_0; a one-layer model never does), so every read inside the build is recorded with the value seen, and each call compares exactly that set against the live sliders: numbers exactly, tensor tables cell by cell against a flat copy. No key string, no allocation on the unchanged path. The generic i.i.d. sampler has its OWN separate cache keyed on dimension only.
implementation.storage: Per layer and per head, typed arrays sized from the configuration in force: Q, K, V and each head's output as Float64Array(n * d_k); S, S_scaled and A as Float64Array(n * n); the residual stream, its increments and the concatenated heads as Float64Array(n * d_model) and Float64Array(n * n_heads * d_k); the FFN hidden layer as Float64Array(n * d_ff); logits and probabilities as Float64Array(n * vocab). Weights are nested arrays (rows of columns). At the toy shape that is 12 numbers per projection and 36 per score table.
implementation.general_engine: Configuration comes from the embedding table in force (tf_emb of any shape, else the scene-4 alias s4_emb over the toy table: rows = n, columns = d_model) and the scalar sliders tf_layers (1), tf_heads (2), tf_kv (= n_heads; 1 is MQA), tf_dk (d_model / n_heads), tf_dff (2 d_model), tf_norm (0 none — the toy, 1 LayerNorm, 2 RMSNorm), tf_prenorm (1 pre-norm, 0 post-norm), tf_act (0 ReLU, 1 GELU, 2 SwiGLU), tf_temp (1). Per layer l: pre-norm normalises what a sub-layer READS and adds its raw output; post-norm adds first and normalises the sum. Attention: every head h reads K/V head floor(h / (n_heads / n_kv)); scores use (sqrt d_k)^s3_scale; the causal mask and its mask-after-softmax misconception follow s3_mask / s3_maskafter in every head; heads are concatenated (n_heads x d_k) and projected by W_O back to d_model. FFN: d_model -> d_ff -> d_model with the chosen activation (SwiGLU gates silu(x W1) by x W3). After the last layer, pre-norm applies a final norm; logits are the tied unembedding (each vocabulary entry's embedding row) and probabilities are softmax(logits / tf_temp). Weights: layer 0 / head 0 is the hand-built toy when d_model = 4 and d_k = 2, every other table is a seeded N(0, 1/rows) initialisation, and any table is replaced cell-wise by a tensor slider named tf_wq_<l>_<h>, tf_wk_<l>_<g>, tf_wv_<l>_<g>, tf_wo_<l>, tf_w1_<l>, tf_w2_<l>, tf_w3_<l> or tf_emb (s4_wq / s4_wk / s4_wv / s4_emb alias layer 0 / head 0 and the table).

verified_values.note: Every figure below is asserted by scripts/check_transformer_domain.py. If a change breaks one, the lesson's arithmetic is wrong, not the test.
verified_values.mask_after_softmax_row2_sum: 0.989933 — the visible failure of applying the mask in the wrong place
verified_values.permutation_equivariance: tfOutNoPos with shuffle on equals the shuffle-off rows reordered by [5,0,3,2,1,4], max deviation 2.2e-16

note: MOST functions read slider state at call time — either by ID directly, or through the cached forward pass _st(), which is rebuilt when any slider it read changes: s1_shuffle, s1_pe, s2_rope, s3_scale, s3_mask, s3_maskafter, the tf_* configuration sliders, and every weight-override tensor slider (tf_wq_<l>_<h> ... and the scene-4 aliases s4_emb, s4_wq, s4_wk, s4_wv), each of which defaults to the hand-built or seeded table when the scene does not declare it. Eight are PURE in their explicit arguments and consult no slider at all: tfPE, tfRopeQ, tfRopeK, tfRopeDot, tfRopeEmbTheta, tfDotSample, tfDotSampleScaled and tfSampleVar. Note tfRopeEmbDot is NOT among them — it reaches _st() through tfRopeEmb. The scene must define sliders with the IDs listed in sliderContracts for the lesson to respond to user input. Functions clamp their index arguments, so an out-of-range row or column returns an edge value rather than NaN.

s1_shuffle.description: Token shuffle. 0 = original order 'the cat sat on the mat'; 1 = permuted by [5,0,3,2,1,4]. Positions never shuffle — only the tokens sitting in them.

s1_pe.description: Additive sinusoidal positional-encoding strength. 0 = embeddings only (position-free); 1 = full sinusoidal PE added. Continuous so the student can watch the points travel rather than jump. IGNORED (treated as 0) while s2_rope = 1 — RoPE replaces additive PE rather than stacking on it.

s2_rope.description: RoPE on/off. When 1, Q and K are rotated by position*theta. V is NEVER rotated — accuracy-contract item 7. RoPE and additive sinusoidal PE are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE: with this on, s1_pe is forced to 0 and the layer input is the raw embedding, so position enters exactly once, as a rotation of q and k.

s2_m.description: RoPE query position m for the standalone demo vector.

s2_n.description: RoPE key position n for the standalone demo vector. Only m-n affects the score.

s2_qdir.description: Exploratory query rotation in degrees, for tfQProbe. A what-if direction, NOT the model's own query — the scene must label it as such.

s3_qi.description: Which query row i is being computed and highlighted. Default 2 = 'sat', the flagship row.

s3_scale.description: Scaling exponent. Scores are divided by (sqrt d_k)^s3_scale, so 0 = no scaling and 1 = the correct 1/sqrt(d_k). Continuous so the row visibly relaxes.

s3_mask.description: Causal mask on/off. 0 = bidirectional (every token sees every token); 1 = causal.

s3_maskafter.description: Mask placement. 0 = CORRECT (additive -1e9 on the scores, before softmax); 1 = WRONG (softmax first, then zero the future with no renormalization), which makes row 2 sum to 0.989933. For the misconception beat only.

s3_gen_d.description: Dimension n of the GENERIC i.i.d. random vectors used by the variance argument. This is a DIFFERENT object from the toy model, whose hand-constructed Q/K do not satisfy the i.i.d. hypothesis. Labelled on screen as 'generic dimension n (NOT our d_k)'.

s4_emb.description: Sandbox override for the whole embedding table W_E (6 token rows x 4 components), one tensor slider. Absent, the hand-built table stands; a scene that declares it must default it to that table. Rows 0 and 4 are both 'the' and start identical; editing one alone makes the two 'the's differ, which the sandbox may do on purpose.

s4_wq.description: Sandbox override for the projection W_Q (4 input dims x 2 head dims), one tensor slider; rows index the input dimension, columns the head dimension. Absent, the hand-built matrix stands; a scene that declares it must default it to that matrix.

s4_wk.description: Sandbox override for the projection W_K (4 input dims x 2 head dims), one tensor slider; rows index the input dimension, columns the head dimension. Absent, the hand-built matrix stands; a scene that declares it must default it to that matrix.

s4_wv.description: Sandbox override for the projection W_V (4 input dims x 2 head dims), one tensor slider; rows index the input dimension, columns the head dimension. Absent, the hand-built matrix stands; a scene that declares it must default it to that matrix.

tf_layers.description: Number of layers in the stack (1..12). Default 1: the toy. tfH(l) is the stream entering layer l; tfH(tf_layers) leaves it.

tf_heads.description: Number of query heads (1..64). Default 2. d_k defaults to d_model / n_heads; heads beyond head 0 use seeded weights unless a tf_wq_<l>_<h> slider replaces them.

tf_kv.description: Number of K/V heads (1..n_heads). Default n_heads (multi-head). 1 is multi-query attention: every query head reads the same K and V; n_heads / n_kv query heads share each K/V head (grouped-query in between). tfKvSaving() = n_heads / n_kv.

tf_dk.description: Per-head dimension. Default d_model / n_heads (a convention, not a law). Layer 0 / head 0 keeps the hand-built projections only while d_model = 4 and d_k = 2.

tf_dff.description: FFN hidden width. Default 2 d_model = 8 (real models use 4x, or 8/3 x for SwiGLU).

tf_norm.description: 0 = no normalisation anywhere (the toy of scenes 1-4), 1 = LayerNorm (subtract the mean, divide by the standard deviation), 2 = RMSNorm (divide by the root mean square only: no mean, no bias). Unit gain, zero bias in both.

tf_prenorm.description: Where a norm (tf_norm 1 or 2) sits. 1 = pre-norm: each sub-layer reads the normed stream and adds its raw output, and a final norm precedes the unembedding. 0 = post-norm: add first, then normalise the sum; no final norm. Ignored while tf_norm = 0.

tf_act.description: FFN activation: 0 ReLU, 1 GELU (tanh approximation), 2 SwiGLU (silu(x W1) * (x W3), then W2).

tf_temp.description: Softmax temperature for the next-token distribution: tfProb = softmax(logits / T). T -> 0 is argmax, T -> infinity is uniform. Never applied to attention.

tf_emb.description: The embedding table, of ANY shape: rows are the tokens, columns d_model. Declaring it reshapes the whole model (n and d_model follow it; tokens beyond the toy's six are named t0, t1, ...). Absent, s4_emb over the toy table stands.

tf_wq_<l>_<h>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). W_Q of layer l, query head h (d_model x d_k). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

tf_wk_<l>_<g>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). W_K of layer l, K/V head g (d_model x d_k). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

tf_wv_<l>_<g>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). W_V of layer l, K/V head g (d_model x d_k). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

tf_wo_<l>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). W_O of layer l (n_heads d_k x d_model). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

tf_w1_<l>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). FFN W1 of layer l (d_model x d_ff). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

tf_w2_<l>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). FFN W2 of layer l (d_ff x d_model). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

tf_w3_<l>.description: Weight override, cell-wise (a short table overrides the cells it covers). FFN gate W3 of layer l (d_model x d_ff), read only when tf_act = 2 (SwiGLU). Absent, the hand-built table (layer 0 / head 0 at the toy shape) or the seeded initialisation stands.

functions.tfPerm(k): Source token index displayed at slot k. Identity when s1_shuffle=0.
functions.tfEmb(i,d): Component d (0..3) of the raw embedding at slot i, shuffle applied, NO positional encoding.
functions.tfEmbBase(r,d): Component d of embedding TOKEN row r (0..5, no shuffle) as currently in force: the hand-built table unless the tensor slider s4_emb overrides it (cell [r][d]). Use it to draw the embedding table itself; tfEmb(i,d) is the per-SLOT read with the shuffle applied.
functions.tfW(m,r,c): Layer-0 / head-0 shorthand for tfWq / tfWk / tfWv: entry (r, c) of a projection matrix in force: m = 0 for W_Q, 1 for W_K, 2 for W_V; r is the input dim (0..3), c the head dim (0..1), row-vector convention q = x W_Q. The hand-built value unless the tensor slider s4_wq / s4_wk / s4_wv (for m = 0 / 1 / 2) overrides cell [r][c]. Use it to draw the three matrices as lattices.
functions.tfPE(i,d): Component d of the sinusoidal positional encoding for POSITION i. Never shuffles. The position argument is CONTINUOUS — it is neither rounded to a slot nor clamped to N-1 — so a scene can sweep it and watch dims 0 and 1 trace the unit circle sin(p), cos(p). Integer slot arguments are unaffected.
functions.tfX(i,d): Layer input x_i = tfEmb(i,d) + s1_pe * tfPE(i,d) — except when s2_rope = 1, where the additive term is forced off and x_i = tfEmb(i,d) exactly. RoPE replaces additive PE; the two are never summed.
functions.tfOutNoPos(i,d): Component d (0..1) of UNMASKED, POSITION-FREE attention over the raw embeddings. The permutation-equivariance object and nothing else — computed by a separate pass, because reusing the masked one would silently break the theorem. Still scaled dot-product attention, so it divides by sqrt(d_k).
functions.tfQ(i,d): q_i = x_i W_Q for head 0, RoPE applied when s2_rope=1 — in which case x_i carries no additive PE, because RoPE replaces it.
functions.tfK(i,d): k_i = x_i W_K, RoPE applied when s2_rope=1.
functions.tfV(i,d): v_i = x_i W_V. NEVER rotated by RoPE.
functions.tfQProbe(d,angleDeg): Component d of the query at slot s3_qi rotated by angleDeg in the head plane. An exploratory what-if; angleDeg=0 returns tfQ(s3_qi,d) exactly.
functions.tfScoreDiv(i,j,dim): tfScore(i,j) / sqrt(dim), with dim passed LITERALLY by the scene: 2 is d_k (correct), 4 is d_model (the classic error). Passing it literally keeps the wrongness explicit in the JSON rather than hidden in a slider.
functions.tfMaskVal(i,j): 1 if j<=i else 0; all 1 when s3_mask=0.
functions.tfAttn(i,j): The final attention weight, honouring s3_scale, s3_mask and s3_maskafter.
functions.tfRowSum(i): Sum over j of tfAttn(i,j). THE accuracy-contract-item-1 assertion. Render with toFixed(tfRowSum(i), 6) so 0.989933 is unmistakable against 1.000000.
functions.tfOut(i,d): o_i = sum_j tfAttn(i,j) v_j — a convex combination of the value rows.
functions.tfRopeQ(d,m): Component d of R_m q for the standalone demo vector q=[0.6,-1.3], theta=1.0.
functions.tfRopeK(d,n): Component d of R_n k for k=[-0.9,0.4], theta=1.0.
functions.tfRopeEmb(slot,d,p): Component d of the RoPE-rotated EMBEDDING of the token at slot `slot`, placed at CONTINUOUS position p. A CONCEPTUAL picture for scene 1, NOT the model's own arithmetic: real RoPE is applied to q and k AFTER the projections and never to the embedding or to v (accuracy-contract item 7). d_model = 4 gives exactly two dimension pairs, (0,1) and (2,3), and each is rotated INDEPENDENTLY at its own rate, so the result is not one rotation of one 4-vector and its 3-D projection does not close into a circle. Both pair norms (and the full norm) are preserved at every p. A pair that is zero in the embedding stays zero: slot 5 ('mat') is the only row in the table with BOTH pairs non-zero, so it is the only one that shows the two-frequency effect. Any scene using this MUST label the frequencies as illustrative and state the real schedule.
functions.tfRopeEmbTheta(pair): The ILLUSTRATIVE rotation rate tfRopeEmb uses for dimension pair 0 or 1, in radians per position: 1.0 and 0.35. These are NOT the real schedule, which is theta_i = 10000^(-2i/d_model) = 1.0 and 0.01 at d_model = 4 — the second pair would move 0.06 rad over the whole six-token sentence, the trajectory would look like a single planar rotation, and the picture would teach the misconception it exists to prevent. Exposed so a scene can display the number it is actually drawing with.
functions.tfRopeDot(m,n): <R_m q, R_n k>. Depends only on m-n; that identity IS proof 3, made draggable.
functions.tfRopeEmbDot(slotA,pa,slotB,pb): The full d_model-dimensional dot product of two RoPE-rotated embeddings. THE RELATIVE-POSITION IDENTITY: each dimension pair contributes a_i^T R_((pb-pa)*theta_i) b_i, so the whole sum depends on pb - pa ALONE — shift both positions by the same amount and the number does not move (asserted to 1e-12). It is the FULL dot product over all d_model coordinates; a scene drawing only three of them is showing a projection, whose own dot product is equal to this one only when the dropped coordinate contributes nothing (e.g. one token is zero in that pair, as 'cat' is). Do not quote this number beside a picture that disagrees with it without saying so.
functions.tfRopeEmbNorm(slot,p): Euclidean norm of a RoPE-rotated embedding. It does NOT depend on p — a rotation is an isometry, so every dimension pair keeps its norm and the vector keeps its length at every position. Exposed as a live quantity precisely so a lesson can show it not moving while the position does.
functions.tfRopeEmbAngle(slotA,pa,slotB,pb): The TRUE angle IN DEGREES between two RoPE-rotated embeddings in the full d_model-dimensional space. Like tfRopeEmbDot it depends on pb - pa ALONE (119.3469 degrees at gap 3 for slots 5 and 0, to 1e-14 across placements). Together with tfRopeEmbNorm it completes Q.K = |Q| |K| cos(theta), which is WHY the dot product is preserved: the two norms are constants of the operation and the angle is fixed by the gap, so the product has no free term left. NOTE this is the angle in R^d_model, NOT the angle between the three-coordinate projections a scene draws — dropping a coordinate shortens one vector more at some positions than others, so the drawn angle can differ by several degrees and is not invariant. A scene printing this beside a projected picture must label which one it is.
functions.tfRopeEmbArc(d,slotA,pa,slotB,pb,s): Component d of the unit-length great-circle (slerp) point at parameter s in [0,1] between two RoPE-rotated embeddings — a DRAWING aid for the angle between them, not part of the forward pass. s=0 and s=1 give the two directions themselves, so any linear projection of the result still lands on the projected direction at the endpoints and a scene can scale it down to draw an arc whose ends sit on the two vectors it spans. The arc's true angular extent is acos of the normalised tfRopeEmbDot and depends only on pb - pa; its projected appearance need not.
functions.tfDotSample(idx,n): q.k for the idx-th deterministic i.i.d. N(0,1) draw pair in R^n. Seeded splitmix32 + Box-Muller, fixed seed, so the scatter is identical on every load and reproducible offline. THE GENERIC OBJECT — nothing to do with the toy model's Q/K.
functions.tfSampleVar(n,count): Empirical variance of the first `count` of 4000 samples at dimension n. The student's own small experiment; the authoritative 2,000,000-draw figures (2.0003 at n=2, 64.10 at n=64) live in the lesson data block and must be labelled as the anchor.
functions.tfToken(k): Token surface form at slot k, as a STRING (e.g. "cat") — TOKENS[tfPerm(k)]. The one function here that returns text rather than a number, for a tensor's axes[].labelExpr: a lattice whose rows permute needs labels that permute with them.
functions.tfScoreProbe(j,angleDeg): Score of the what-if query against key j: q_probe . k_j, where q_probe is slot s3_qi's query turned by angleDeg. Equals tfScore(s3_qi,j) EXACTLY at angleDeg=0, where the probe is the model's own query. Rotates once per call, unlike two tfQProbe reads.
functions.tfProjQK(d,angleDeg,j): Component d of the vector projection of the what-if query onto key j: ((q.k)/(k.k))k. Its signed length times |k_j| IS the score q.k_j, which is what makes the dot product drawable as a length. Returns 0 for a zero-length key, where the projection is undefined.
functions.tfN(): Number of tokens n in force (6 for the toy; the row count of tf_emb otherwise).
functions.tfDModel(): d_model in force (4 for the toy; the column count of tf_emb otherwise).
functions.tfDk(): Per-head dimension d_k in force (tf_dk, default d_model / n_heads).
functions.tfKv(): Number of K/V heads (tf_kv, default n_heads).
functions.tfVocabN(): Vocabulary size: distinct surface forms among the tokens (5 for the toy: the, cat, sat, on, mat).
functions.tfVocabToken(v): Surface form of vocabulary entry v, as a STRING, in first-seen order (the toy: 0 the, 1 cat, 2 sat, 3 on, 4 mat).
functions.tfHeadKv(h): Which K/V head query head h reads: floor(h / (n_heads / n_kv)). Identity under MHA, 0 for every head under MQA.
functions.tfKvCache(): Numbers held in the K/V cache for the whole sequence: 2 n n_kv d_k per layer, summed over layers.
functions.tfKvSaving(): The K/V-cache saving from sharing heads: n_heads / n_kv (1 for MHA, n_heads for MQA).
functions.tfWq(l,h,r,c): W_Q of layer l, query head h, entry (r, c): r the input dim (0..d_model-1), c the head dim (0..d_k-1). Layer 0 / head 0 is the hand-built toy at the toy shape.
functions.tfWk(l,g,r,c): W_K of layer l, K/V head g, entry (r, c).
functions.tfWv(l,g,r,c): W_V of layer l, K/V head g, entry (r, c).
functions.tfWo(l,r,c): W_O of layer l, entry (r, c): r indexes the concatenated heads (0..n_heads d_k - 1, head floor(r / d_k)), c the stream dim.
functions.tfW1(l,r,c): FFN W1 of layer l (d_model x d_ff), entry (r, c).
functions.tfW2(l,r,c): FFN W2 of layer l (d_ff x d_model), entry (r, c).
functions.tfWu(v,d): Row v of the tied unembedding: the embedding row of vocabulary entry v, component d. tfLogit(i, v) = sum_d tfFinal(i, d) tfWu(v, d).
functions.tfH(l,i,d): Component d of the residual stream ENTERING layer l at slot i. l = 0 is x (embedding plus PE); l = tf_layers is what leaves the stack, before the final norm.
functions.tfAttnIn(l,i,d): What the attention sub-layer of layer l reads at slot i: the normed stream (pre-norm) or the stream itself (post-norm).
functions.tfQh(l,h,i,d): q of slot i in layer l, head h, component d (RoPE applied when s2_rope = 1). tfQ = tfQh(0, 0, ...).
functions.tfKh(l,h,i,d): k of slot i as read by head h of layer l (its K/V head's key), component d.
functions.tfVh(l,h,i,d): v of slot i as read by head h of layer l. NEVER rotated by RoPE.
functions.tfScoreH(l,h,i,j): Raw score q_i . k_j in layer l, head h.
functions.tfScoreScaledH(l,h,i,j): Scaled score, tfScoreH / (sqrt d_k)^s3_scale, in layer l, head h.
functions.tfAttnH(l,h,i,j): Attention weight of query slot i on key slot j in layer l, head h, honouring s3_scale, s3_mask and s3_maskafter. Rows sum to 1 (except in the mask-after misconception mode).
functions.tfHeadOut(l,h,i,d): Head h's own output row i, component d (0..d_k-1) in layer l: sum_j tfAttnH(l,h,i,j) tfVh(l,h,j,d) — BEFORE concatenation and W_O. tfOut = tfHeadOut(0, 0, ...).
functions.tfConcat(l,i,c): The concatenated heads of layer l at slot i, column c (0..n_heads d_k - 1); column c belongs to head floor(c / d_k). What W_O multiplies.
functions.tfAttnOut(l,i,d): The attention sub-layer's increment to the stream at slot i: concat times W_O, component d (0..d_model-1). Multi-head does not widen the stream.
functions.tfResid1(l,i,d): The stream after the attention residual add in layer l (post-norm: after its norm).
functions.tfFfIn(l,i,d): What the FFN of layer l reads: the normed stream (pre-norm) or tfResid1 itself (post-norm).
functions.tfFfPre(l,i,k): FFN hidden unit k (0..d_ff-1) at slot i BEFORE the activation: tfFfIn . W1.
functions.tfFfHidden(l,i,k): FFN hidden unit k at slot i after the activation (SwiGLU: silu(x W1) * (x W3)). One neuron's fan-in is row k of W1.
functions.tfFfOut(l,i,d): The FFN's increment to the stream at slot i, component d: tfFfHidden . W2.
functions.tfResid2(l,i,d): The stream LEAVING layer l at slot i (= tfH(l + 1, i, d)); post-norm: after its norm.
functions.tfFinal(i,d): The vector the unembedding reads at slot i: the final norm of the stream leaving the stack (pre-norm) or that stream itself (post-norm).
functions.tfLogit(i,v): Logit of vocabulary entry v at slot i: tfFinal(i, .) dot tfWu(v, .), before temperature.
functions.tfProb(i,v): softmax(logits / tf_temp)[v] at slot i: the model's distribution for the token AFTER slot i (causal). Sums to 1 over v.
functions.tfArgmax(i): Index of the most probable vocabulary entry at slot i (independent of temperature). Feed it to tfVocabToken for the word.
functions.tfEntropy(i): Shannon entropy in bits of the slot-i distribution: -> 0 as tf_temp -> 0, -> log2(tfVocabN()) as tf_temp -> infinity.
